description: Git bulk ops — investigation + workflow combos in one call

git-status.description: Branch, commits + base divergence, changes, stashes, open MR/PR with diff size. A two-sided `ahead N, behind M` gains a `Diverged:` line saying which kind it is — REBASED (every remote commit is patch-equivalent to one you already have; nothing lost, force-with-lease) vs a genuine divergence naming how many remote commits are not in your history, or a stated UNKNOWN when that check did not answer. `:full` (alias `:porcelain`) uncaps every file/branch/stash list — full untruncated view for driving precise staging. `:brief` drops the local-branch inventory and the commit log so the working tree and the MR/PR block sit at the top; a section that could not be read is never dropped. An unrecognised mode is reported, not ignored

git-investigate.description: File history: commits, uncommitted, blame hotspots

git-diff.description: Review-aware diff: classified files + +/-, red-flag scan of added lines (debug code/conflict markers w/ file:line), forbidden-path guard, missing-test pairing, next hints. Add trailing :full (any mode) to append the raw +/- hunks under ## Patch. Policy via .supertool.json ops.git-diff.{red_flags_extra,forbidden_paths,test_pairing,hints}

git-blame.description: Git blame N lines around LINE

git-checkout.description: Switch to REF — branch, tracking, dirty, last commits

git-diverge.description: Branch vs base — ahead/behind, commits, files, +/- totals

git-merge.description: Merge REF — on conflict: UU files, markers, ours/theirs SHAs

git-conflicts.description: List UU files + every conflict block + abort hint

git-resolve.description: Pick ours/theirs/both(union) for PATH (single, comma-separated list, or 'all') + stage + continue cmd. Optional 1-indexed BLOCKS selector (single file) resolves only those conflict blocks (as git-conflicts numbers them); a partial resolve keeps the other blocks' markers and stays unstaged ('N of M blocks resolved'). 'both' is REFUSED per file on source extensions (.py/.js/.php/.sh/... — a union concatenates two versions of code, the result parses, the block runs twice): the file is left conflicted, the tally reads 'Refused: N', and a mixed set still resolves its non-source files. Ways through: append 'force' (the tally then discloses how many source files were unioned), or declare the path merge=union in .gitattributes, which is honoured without a flag. 'both' is ALSO refused on a Markdown file when the union would DUPLICATE A HEADING — the same heading line on both sides of one hunk, which a line-level union emits twice and which reparents every line between the two copies under the first (a Keep a Changelog release heading turns unreleased entries into shipped ones). The refusal names the heading; only 'force' gets through, merge=union does not, and an ordinary changelog conflict (two bullets under a shared heading) is untouched
git-resolve.syntax: git-resolve:::SIDE:::PATH[,PATH...][:::BLOCKS][:::force]  (SIDE: ours|theirs|both; BLOCKS: e.g. 1,3 — single file only; force: union source files anyway)

git-worktrees.description: Is an agent working in this worktree? Answers OWNERSHIP for every worktree (or one PATH): branch, path, merged-into-base, and an occupancy verdict in THREE states — `occupied`, `idle`, and `cannot tell` — each naming the evidence it was built from. `cannot tell` is the honest majority answer and is NOT `idle`: liveness is undecidable, and a checker that guesses `idle` when it could not look reproduces the incident this op exists for (`ps aux | grep <worktree path>` returns 0 for a live agent — the path is in the process's *cwd*, never in its argv). `idle` therefore has to be earned: every probe must have answered — the tree stat'd and quiet, AND the process table read and holding nobody. Signals: index.lock/HEAD.lock, a rebase/merge/cherry-pick in progress, `git worktree lock` (git's own announce mechanism, read rather than reinvented), newest write inside the activity window (SUPERTOOL_WORKTREE_ACTIVE_WINDOW, default 900s; `idle` additionally requires quiet for SUPERTOOL_WORKTREE_IDLE_QUIET, default 3600s, because worktrees were observed being edited with no process chdir'd into them), and a process whose cwd is inside the tree (/proc on Linux, `lsof -d cwd` elsewhere — absent on Windows, which declines by name). INSPECTION ONLY: nothing is removed, pruned, unlocked or written, and no removal command is ever printed. With a PATH, exit 0 only for `idle` (1 occupied, 2 cannot tell), so `cannot tell` cannot collapse into either neighbour. Each row also names its branch's TRACKER state, in FOUR states that must not collapse either: `PR #N` with the check tally summed off the same call, `no open PR` (asked, and nothing tracks a branch that is pushed), `no remote ref` (never pushed, or the remote branch was deleted — the two leave the same local trace, so both are named), and `PR unknown` (the lookup did not run: offline, unauthenticated, rate-limited, not a GitHub remote, or the open-PR page hit its cap — NEVER rendered as `no open PR`, which would read as unpublished work in the op you use to pick a tree). ONE `gh pr list` call for N worktrees, not N. On by default; `nopr` or SUPERTOOL_WORKTREE_PR=0 turns it off and the op is then fully offline. The exit code stays a statement about occupancy alone.

git-commit.description: Commit MESSAGE (stages PATHS) — Repo (which repository this wrote to, stamped before staging so it survives a hook rejection), HEAD before/after, hook errors surfaced. A MESSAGE containing ':' — every Conventional Commits subject — MUST use the triple-colon form or the @payload route: the single-colon CLI splits on every ':' and would hand the tail to `git add` as a pathspec. PATHS are separated by ':::' — not by commas, not by spaces — and both routes stage, the payload one via a `paths` list. MESSAGE=amend (or --amend) is REFUSED: there is no amend route, so committing it made a commit subject-lined 'amend'; use `git commit --amend` directly, or SUPERTOOL_ALLOW_LITERAL_AMEND=1 for the literal subject. A PATH that is neither path-shaped (no whitespace/quotes) nor known to git (on disk, tracked, or an already-staged deletion) is taken as that split and REFUSED before anything is staged, naming both working routes; it is never folded back into the message, because guessing wrong that way commits the already-staged fileset under a mangled subject. A path-shaped PATH git does not know still gets git's own pathspec error. MESSAGE=--no-edit reuses MERGE_MSG/CHERRY_PICK msg (merge or cherry-pick must be in progress). Auto-appends a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer when absent; identity via .supertool.json ops.git-commit.coauthor (default 'Max <noreply>'; set '' / 'none' to disable). Multi-line body: use the @file route — git-commit:@- (stdin) or git-commit:@msg.toml — with a `message` field (subject + blank line + body) and optional `paths` list; the trailer is still appended. Omitting PATHS is refused with the CAUSE, not the symptom (#1155): `no PATHS were given — git-commit never stages for you, so nothing staged`, on the FIRST line, because the `--- op ---` header has already replayed the whole message above it. The other three openings say `the N path(s) you named held no changes`, `the working tree is clean`, or that `git status` did not answer — four situations, four sentences, never one wording for all of them. PATHS=--all is the explicit opt-in (#1137) that accepts the dirty list the refusal just counted (modified tracked + untracked, ignored excluded) instead of sending you to a raw `git status --porcelain` to rebuild it; the receipt then names EVERY path uncapped, since under --all the caller never typed the list. It is refused beside a named path, refused when git knows a file literally called `--all` (use `./--all`), and refused when `git status` did not answer — never resolved into a commit. `paths = ["--all"]` spells the same thing on the @payload route.

git-push.description: Push current branch (sets upstream if missing). ALWAYS ends on a one-line `[result]` verdict — PUSHED / NOT PUSHED (already up to date | REJECTED | REBASE PAUSED | UNVERIFIED | no push attempted) with branch → remote/ref @ sha — so the answer survives `| tail -3`. The post-push sha is read back off the real remote via ls-remote and labelled verified/unverified; a sha that was not read is never printed as if it were. Receipt: Repo (which LOCAL repository these commits came from), remote before/after, ahead/behind, MR/PR + pipeline, mergeability, behind-target, uncommitted-leftover COUNT (list: git-status:full), watch cmd. Non-ff auto-rebases (conflict → paused + git-conflicts). Hook amend+push reported as PUSHED. A push that outlasts its budget is verified against the remote ref before any verdict — landed = PUSHED. A fetch/rebase on the non-fast-forward recovery path that outlasts its own budget reports the WORKTREE state — rebase in progress (with continue/abort), not started, or explicitly unknown — instead of a traceback. The stale-base check follows the branch's real upstream remote (not a hardcoded origin) and says `skipped` when the target ref does not resolve, so silence means only `checked, base is fresh`. On a branch with NO upstream the push remote is RESOLVED, not assumed: branch.<name>.pushRemote, remote.pushDefault, branch.<name>.remote (git's own order), then `origin` if it exists, then the only remote if there is exactly one — so `git clone -o gitlab` and fork/upstream layouts work. Two or more remotes with none named origin and nothing configured is REFUSED (exit 1, nothing pushed) naming the candidates, because creating a branch on a guessed remote is not recoverable by an error message. Flags: :force-with-lease, :no-verify, :watch (spawns a background pipeline poller; falls back to the running interpreter + supertool.py where the ./supertool wrapper is absent, e.g. a git worktree, and names the reason if it cannot start). An UNKNOWN flag is REFUSED before anything is pushed (exit 2) — never silently dropped. An upstream that resolves to a DIFFERENT branch — the default outcome of `git worktree add -b <new> <base>`, so every st-wt/NNN branch starts here — is still refused rather than guessed through, but both ways out are now flags on this op instead of raw `git push` lines the caller's own hook may forbid: `:set-upstream` pushes the branch under its own name and retargets tracking to <remote>/<branch> (the usual first push), `:to-upstream` pushes onto the tracked ref on purpose with an explicit refspec. Asking for both is REFUSED (exit 2) naming the two targets — they are different refs and precedence would be the guess the refusal exists to prevent.
